inspection: Read-only source and completed result inspection
scope: sdk/mutator.ts against tests/mutator_sdk.test.ts; original eleven-test dogfood run retained

runEvidence.warning: The run is incomplete: seventy execution errors and one timeout remain distinct from recognized kills and survivors. Twenty survivors are individually inspectable; this does not establish complete mutation coverage.

proposedControls.notes: Seven concise public-behavior tests. Existing eleven-test evidence is unchanged. Do not assert allocation sizes or conservative encoding arithmetic.

context.after: typeof value !== "object" || types.isProxy(value) || Array.isArray(value)) invalid(`${label} must be a plain object`);

survivors.reason: Removing the non-object check permits a callable value whose own fields and prototype imitate plain request data. Ordinary primitive rejection alone does not exercise this bypass.
survivors.counterexample: Create an arrow function, delete its configurable length/name own properties, set its prototype to Object.prototype, and assign exactly the valid request fields. Original rejects typeof function; mutant reaches all subsequent checks and returns a normalized request.
negativeControls: Normal and null-prototype request records remain accepted. A record with a custom prototype stays rejected.
survivors.recommendation: Add rejection of callable protocol input without calling the function.
proposedControls: callable values cannot impersonate plain request data
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

survivors.reason: The existing fixtures exercise mutation phase with an already valid ID. Inverting this branch rejects valid baseline input and skips validation of mutation IDs.
survivors.counterexample: A baseline request with mutationId=null is valid in the original and rejected by the mutant. A mutation request with a malformed non-SHA256 ID is rejected in the original and accepted by the mutant.
negativeControls: A valid mutation request remains accepted. Baseline with a nonnull ID and unknown phase stay rejected.
survivors.recommendation: Check valid baseline and mutation requests plus malformed phase-dependent IDs.
proposedControls: baseline and mutation requests enforce their distinct mutation identities
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

context.after: limit) invalid("request must be a bounded regular file");

survivors.reason: The public request ceiling is inclusive. Current tests reject 65,537 bytes but never accept 65,536 valid bytes.
survivors.counterexample: Write a valid request with leading JSON whitespace totaling exactly 65,536 bytes and the essential closing brace at the final byte. Original accepts it; metadata.size>=limit rejects it.
negativeControls: 65,537 bytes stays rejected. An ordinary smaller request remains accepted.
survivors.recommendation: Add an exact request ceiling acceptance control and one extra byte rejection.
proposedControls: the request byte ceiling includes an exact-size valid JSON document
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

survivors.reason: Reducing the buffer to limit-1 truncates a valid document at the supported public ceiling. This is observable through the public reader without asserting its allocation strategy.
survivors.counterexample: Use the exact 65,536-byte valid request with the closing brace at the last byte. The limit-1 buffer drops the brace, so JSON parsing rejects a supported document.
negativeControls: A smaller request remains accepted. A file over the public ceiling stays rejected.
survivors.recommendation: Reuse the public exact-byte-ceiling control; do not assert buffer allocation.
proposedControls: the request byte ceiling includes an exact-size valid JSON document
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

survivors.reason: For a stable regular file, fstat rejects oversize files before reading, and a limit-sized buffer still accepts every permitted byte count. This is stable-file equivalence only. The extra byte also detects growth after fstat; that race was not exercised by the current tests.
survivors.counterexample: No stable-file public counterexample. If the same open file grows after fstat and begins with a complete valid limit-byte JSON prefix, the mutant can stop before the extra byte and miss the growth. This is an unexecuted race hypothesis.
negativeControls: Exact permitted bytes and one extra stable byte are covered by the proposed public boundary control. Existing symlink and excessive-file controls remain relevant.
survivors.recommendation: Do not assert the internal allocation. Retain the qualified equivalence and note that a future deterministic real-file growth control could assess the bounded-reader race separately.
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

survivors.reason: For an ordinary regular-file read, the changed loop can perform one extra zero-length read after filling the buffer. That read returns zero and breaks; returned bytes and the subsequent byte-limit decision remain the same.
survivors.counterexample: No public behavior counterexample under the supported ordinary file-read contract. Changing a mocked zero-length read to return nonzero would test the mock instead of this contract.
negativeControls: Short reads, ordinary EOF, exact request bytes, and over-ceiling bytes retain the same public outcome.
survivors.recommendation: Document this survivor; add no private call-count assertion.
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

negativeControls: One extra stable byte stays rejected. An ordinary smaller request remains accepted.

context.after: !path.isAbsolute(assigned)) invalid("ARCHGUARD_MUTATION_REQUEST must name an absolute file");

survivors.reason: Changing OR to AND skips the absolute-path requirement whenever the assigned environment value is nonempty.
survivors.counterexample: Assign an existing valid request file through path.relative(process.cwd(),requestFile). Original rejects the relative path; mutant opens the same file and accepts the request.
negativeControls: An absolute path to that same file remains accepted. Assigned result identity and existing symlink rejection remain checked.
survivors.recommendation: Check a real relative path, then restore the absolute assignment and both environment variables.
proposedControls: assigned request files require absolute paths even when a relative file exists
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

survivors.reason: Current requests are minified, so the whitespace-skipping update is not exercised. Valid JSON formatting is part of the reader contract.
survivors.counterexample: A valid request with leading newline/tab and pretty-printed key spacing is accepted by the original. The mutant moves offset backward when it meets whitespace, so the sticky token scan cannot consume the document correctly.
negativeControls: A minified request still works. A repeated key using an escaped spelling request\u0049d stays rejected after JSON key decoding.
survivors.recommendation: Add formatted JSON acceptance, an escaped duplicate-key rejection, and a corrected minified request.
proposedControls: formatted request JSON is accepted while escaped duplicate keys remain rejected
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

context.after: (result.exitCode as number) < 0 || (result.exitCode as number) > 255) invalid("exitCode must be a process exit code");

survivors.reason: The first changed logical operator weakens the independent integer check. The existing suite exercises only integer exit codes 0 and 1.
survivors.counterexample: A result with exitCode=1.5, otherwise a valid completed result without failures, is rejected by the original and accepted by the mutant. NaN also bypasses the mutant comparisons.
negativeControls: Integer exit codes 0, 1, and 255 remain accepted. Negative and above-255 values must be rejected.
survivors.recommendation: Check process-code integer and range requirements through validateMutationResult.
proposedControls: result exit codes accept integer endpoints and reject values outside the process range
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

context.after: (result.exitCode as number) > 255) invalid("exitCode must be a process exit code");

survivors.reason: The second changed logical operator combines the two mutually exclusive range failures, weakening both range checks for integer values.
survivors.counterexample: exitCode=-1 or 256 is rejected by the original. In the mutant, an integer cannot be simultaneously below zero and above 255, so either value is accepted.
negativeControls: Integer endpoints 0 and 255 remain accepted. A fractional value stays rejected by the remaining integer check.
survivors.recommendation: Use the same public exit-code boundary control.
proposedControls: result exit codes accept integer endpoints and reject values outside the process range
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

context.after: 255) invalid("exitCode must be a process exit code");

survivors.reason: The public process-code range includes 255. The current suite never checks that endpoint.
survivors.counterexample: exitCode=255 with otherwise valid result data is accepted by the original and rejected by the mutant.
negativeControls: 0 and 1 remain accepted. -1, 256, fractions, strings, null, NaN, and infinity remain rejected.
survivors.recommendation: Use the same public exit-code boundary control.
proposedControls: result exit codes accept integer endpoints and reject values outside the process range
survivors.verification: Source reasoning only; this inspection did not execute original or mutated code.

context.after: failureValues.length !== 0)) invalid("exit zero disagrees with failures");

survivors.reason: The current contradictory-exit test has both a failed assertion count and a failure record. AND and OR give the same result in that fixture. Hook-only failures can have zero failed test IDs.
survivors.counterexample: A complete exit-zero result with passed=1, failed=0 and one hook failure with testId=null passes failed-ID consistency. Original rejects the contradictory exit status; mutant accepts it because counts.failed is zero.
negativeControls: The same hook-only result with exitCode=1 is accepted. An exit-zero result with no failures remains accepted.
survivors.recommendation: Add a completed hook-only exit-zero rejection and corrected nonzero result.
proposedControls: a completed hook-only failure cannot declare exit zero
